confirm.text: Not the mis-selection pattern — carried-forward selections. 1099 Rolando Flores's two forms carry byte-identical "What did we observe?" selections, an identical "What Did We Observe? Continued" narrative, identical "What went well?" selections and an identical "What Went Well? Continued" narrative across two different wells several hours apart. Brianda Sandoval filed one rig check (Ovintiv, H&P 551 Fasken, job 35098) with all photos current, alarms and lights tested Yes, and the only comment describing work she completed. 1099 Rolando Flores's Trailer Inspection Form for trailer 601 is clean — FR answered Yes, all twelve photos taken on 09/27, comments N/A — although his other four submissions carry the items listed above. Stefanie Kirschke's two air job forms (35097_1 and 35102_1) are clean, with all photos current, both OWL sections completed and narratives written fresh for each job; her Trailer Inspection Form is the FR exception at ite

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so this review can confirm that a photo was taken and when, but not what it shows. Where a form carries an explicit calibration question — "Personal 4 Gas Monitor Calibrated?" on the H2S daily — all three answered Yes.

Second point, about this run rather than the forms: this routine is scheduled for 11:00 PM Central but fired at 5:34 AM Central on Monday 09/28. The day reviewed is therefore the most recently completed Central calendar day, Sunday 09/27/2026, not the day the run started. One consequence worth knowing: 1099 Benjamin Boutte's supervision job 34981_2 closed out at 09/28 01:53 AM, but its final working shift ran from 09/27 04:47 PM. It carries a 09/28 form date, so it is not counted toward 09/27's coverage, but it was read and its content is reflected above.

19 of 19 submissions read. The job board was available: the 9/27/2026 Ark-La-Tex & Permian Basin boards from Blake Walton, received 09/27 at 09:20 AM Central, and the 9-27 sheet of each was used. 18 manned board rows were checked for coverage, 12 on the Permian Basin board and 6 on the ArkLaTex board. The volume is well below a weekday's 45 to 70 — the search was paged to exhaustion and returned nothing beyond these 19, and the board corroborates a quiet Sunday, with most Permian technicians on DAYS OFF and five further rows marked ON STANDBY. A second search across Monday morning was run to catch late arrivals; it returned five forms, four of them carrying 09/28 form dates and belonging to Monday, plus the Boutte close-out described above.
